name: Quebec: language of government services
description: Since 1 June 2023 Quebec's civil administration must serve the public exclusively in French unless an exception applies; immigrants may be served in another language only during their first six months in Quebec.

attributes.jurisdiction: Quebec (provincial bodies, municipalities and other 'civil administration' bodies; federal services are not covered)
attributes.legal_status: in force since 2023-06-01 (Charter of the French language as amended by Bill 96, S.Q. 2022, c. 14, assented 2022-06-01)
attributes.rule: Services exclusively in French unless the body is authorised to use another language and chooses to do so.
exceptions: Immigrants: another language may be used, in addition to French, for integration services during the first six months after arrival in Quebec
Holders of a certificate of eligibility for instruction in English (and persons who dealt with a body only in English before 13 May 2021) may be served in English
Indigenous peoples; tourism services; services outside Quebec; certain enterprises without a Quebec establishment
attributes.excluded_from_english_exception: Children of temporary residents (foreign students, temporary foreign workers) who hold a temporary authorization for English instruction do not thereby gain the right to English communications
attributes.practical_effect: A newcomer should expect French-only correspondence from provincial and municipal bodies after six months, unless covered by an exception.
attributes.status_dependency: Matters only if Quebec is in scope (USER-PROFILE.md: 'English-only vs bilingual environment' unknown) and depends on the user's status and French ability (unknown).

sources.title: Use of a language other than French by the civil administration (last update 5 October 2026)
Bill 96, An Act respecting French, the official and common language of Québec — passed 24 May 2022, assented 1 June 2022 (S.Q. 2022, c. 14) (via search extract)

limitations: Health and public-safety situations are not listed on the page read; the Charter regulation on those cases was not read.
